name: Beef and bean nachos
blurb: Spiced mince and beans over corn chips, topped with cheese and a quick salsa.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Finely chop the onion. Dice the fresh tomatoes and avocado, squeeze over half the lime and season: that's your salsa.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion for 3 minutes until soft.
Add the mince and break it up. Cook until browned all over.
Stir in the taco seasoning, drained beans and canned tomatoes. Simmer until thick.
Spread the corn chips over a big oven tray, spoon the mince over and scatter with cheese. Bake until the cheese melts.
Top with salsa and sour cream and serve straight from the tray.

name: Honey soy chicken with rice and greens
blurb: Sticky glazed chicken thighs with fluffy rice and garlicky greens.
steps: Rinse the rice, then put it in a pot with 2¼ cups of water and a pinch of salt. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on low.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces. Mix the soy, honey, crushed garlic and ginger in a cup.
Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat. Cook the chicken until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the honey soy and let it bubble until sticky and glossy.
Meanwhile cut the broccoli into florets and trim the beans. Steam or microwave them until just tender.
Fluff the rice, pile on the chicken and greens, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

name: Family spaghetti bolognese
blurb: The classic: a rich tomato mince sauce with hidden veg, over spaghetti.
steps: Finely chop the onion and garlic. Grate the carrot and courgette (the kids won't spot them).
Heat the oil in a big pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and courgette until soft.
Turn up the heat, add the mince and garlic, and brown well.
Stir in the tomato paste, passata, oregano and ½ cup water. Season, then simmer with the lid half on.
While it simmers, boil a big pot of salted water and cook the spaghetti.
Drain the pasta, toss with a ladle of sauce, then serve with more sauce and parmesan on top.

name: Oven fish and chips with slaw
blurb: Crumbed fish and crunchy wedges from the oven, with a lemony coleslaw.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with the oil and salt on a tray, and roast.
Set up three plates: flour, beaten egg, panko. Pat the fish dry, then coat each piece in flour, egg, then panko.
When the wedges have had 20 minutes, put the fish on a lined tray with a drizzle of oil and bake alongside.
Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot, and toss with the mayo and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve the fish and chips with slaw, lemon wedges and tomato sauce.

name: Easy butter chicken
blurb: A mild, creamy curry with tender chicken, rice and warm naan.
steps: Start the rice: rinse, add 2¼ cups water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low.
Dice the onion and cut the chicken into chunks.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic and ginger until soft.
Add the curry paste and cook until fragrant, then add the chicken and stir to coat.
Pour in the tomatoes, simmer until the chicken is cooked, then stir through the cream.
Warm the naan in the oven or a dry pan. Serve the curry over rice with coriander on top.

name: Sausage and vege tray bake
blurb: Sausages roasted with kūmara, onion and capsicum, all on one tray.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the kūmara into chunks, the onion into wedges and the capsicums into strips.
Toss the vege with the oil, paprika and salt on a big tray. Nestle the sausages in between.
Roast, turning the sausages once halfway.
Add the broccoli florets for the last few minutes so they char a little.
Serve straight from the tray with relish.

name: Crispy chicken wraps
blurb: Golden chicken strips in soft wraps with crunchy salad and sauces.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Beat the egg in one bowl and put the panko in another.
Dip each tenderloin in egg then panko, lay on a lined tray and drizzle with oil. Bake until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile shred the lettuce and slice the tomato and cucumber.
Warm the wraps for a few seconds in the microwave.
Put everything on the table and let everyone build their own.

name: Baked mac and cheese with peas
blurb: Creamy cheesy macaroni with peas, baked with a crunchy top.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cook the macaroni in boiling salted water until just tender, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a pot, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk and stir until thick and smooth.
Off the heat, stir in 1½ cups of cheese and the mustard. Season.
Mix the drained pasta and peas through the sauce, pour into a dish, top with the rest of the cheese and panko, and bake until golden.

name: Beef and vege noodle stir-fry
blurb: Tender beef strips, crunchy vege and noodles in a savoury sauce.
steps: Slice the capsicum and carrot into thin strips, quarter the bok choy, and crush the garlic. Mix the oyster and soy sauces with 2 tbsp water.
Soak the noodles in hot water to loosen, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the beef in two batches until browned, then set aside.
Stir-fry the vege and garlic until just tender.
Return the beef, add the noodles and sauce, and toss until everything is hot and glossy.
Serve straight away.

name: Shepherd's pie
blurb: Savoury lamb mince under fluffy cheesy mash.
steps: Peel and chop the potatoes and boil until soft.
Meanwhile dice the onion and carrots. Brown the mince in a large pan, then add the onion and carrot and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire and stock. Simmer until thick, then add the peas.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Mash the potatoes with the butter and milk, and season.
Put the mince in a baking dish, spread the mash on top, scatter with cheese and bake until golden.

name: Homemade pizza night
blurb: Ready-made bases with everyone's favourite toppings.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Slice the capsicum and mushrooms, drain the pineapple and chop the ham.
Lay out the bases and toppings so everyone can make their own.
Spread each base with sauce, add cheese and toppings.
Bake until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are crisp.
Serve with a simple green salad.

name: Salmon with crispy potatoes and greens
blurb: Pan-seared salmon with smashed baby potatoes and lemony greens.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Boil the potatoes until tender.
Drain, squash each one flat on an oiled tray, drizzle with oil and salt, and roast until crispy.
Season the salmon. Cook skin-side down in a hot pan until the skin is crisp, then turn and cook to your liking.
In the same pan, add the butter, garlic and greens and toss until just tender.
Squeeze lemon over everything and serve.

name: Chicken and vege noodle soup
blurb: A warming bowl of chicken, vegetables and soft noodles.
steps: Dice the onion, carrots and celery and crush the garlic.
Put the chicken, vege and stock in a big pot. Bring to the boil, then simmer gently.
Lift out the chicken and shred it with two forks.
Add the noodles and corn to the pot and cook until the noodles are soft.
Return the chicken, season, and serve with parsley on top.

name: Sunday roast lamb with veges
blurb: Roast leg of lamb with rosemary, roast vege, peas and gravy.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Make small cuts in the lamb and push in slivers of garlic and rosemary. Rub with oil and salt.
Roast the lamb (about 30 minutes per 500 g for medium).
Cut the potatoes, kūmara and pumpkin into chunks, toss in oil and roast in the last hour.
Rest the lamb under foil while you cook the peas and make the gravy.
Carve and serve with the vege, peas, gravy and mint sauce.

name: Egg fried rice with vege
blurb: Day-old rice tossed with egg, vege and soy. Great for using up leftovers.
steps: Slice the spring onions. Beat the eggs.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set, then push to one side.
Add the frozen vege and stir-fry until hot.
Add the rice, break up any lumps, and stir-fry until heated through and a little crispy.
Add the soy, sesame oil and spring onions, toss well and serve.

name: Chicken burrito bowls
blurb: Spiced chicken over rice with beans, corn, salsa and avocado.
steps: Cook the rice: rinse, add 2¼ cups water and salt, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low.
Toss the chicken in the seasoning and oil. Cook in a hot pan until cooked through, then slice.
Warm the beans and corn together in a small pot.
Dice the tomato and red onion and mix with lime juice for a salsa. Slice the avocado.
Build bowls: rice, chicken, beans and corn, salsa, avocado, cheese and sour cream.

name: Fluffy pancakes with berries
blurb: Thick, fluffy pancakes with berries, yoghurt and maple syrup.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs and milk, then stir into the dry mix until just combined. A few lumps are fine.
Heat a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Pour in ¼ cups of batter and cook until bubbles appear.
Flip and cook the other side until golden.
Keep going with the rest of the batter. Serve stacked with berries, yoghurt and maple syrup.

name: Weekend big breakfast
blurb: Eggs, bacon, mushrooms, tomatoes and toast.
steps: Heat the oven to 100°C to keep things warm. Halve the tomatoes and slice the mushrooms.
Fry the bacon until crisp, then keep warm in the oven.
In the same pan, cook the mushrooms and tomatoes until soft.
Fry or scramble the eggs.
Toast the bread and serve everything together.

name: Overnight oats jars
blurb: Made the night before: oats, milk and yoghurt with fruit on top.
steps: Mix the oats, milk, yoghurt and honey.
Spoon into four jars, top with berries and put in the fridge overnight.
In the morning, add sliced banana and eat cold, or warm for a minute.

name: Banana muffins
blurb: Soft muffins using up brown bananas. Good for breakfasts and lunchboxes.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mash the bananas, then mix in the melted butter, egg, sugar and milk.
Fold in the flour and baking powder until just combined.
Spoon into the tin and bake until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool on a rack. They freeze well.

name: Ham and cheese toasties with soup
blurb: Golden toasted sandwiches with a cup of tomato soup.
steps: Heat the soup gently in a pot.
Butter the outsides of the bread. Fill with ham and cheese.
Cook in a pan or sandwich press until golden and melted.
Cut into triangles and serve with the soup.

name: Easy sushi rolls
blurb: Simple rolls with tuna, cucumber and avocado. Great for lunchboxes.
steps: Rinse the rice well, then cook with 2½ cups water.
Spread the rice in a dish, stir in the sushi seasoning and let it cool.
Mix the tuna with the mayo. Slice the cucumber and avocado into thin sticks.
Lay a nori sheet shiny side down, spread a thin layer of rice, leaving a strip at the top. Add a line of fillings.
Roll up tightly, wet the top strip to seal, and slice with a wet knife. Serve with soy sauce.

name: Chicken salad wraps
blurb: Leftover or rotisserie chicken in a wrap with crunchy salad.
steps: Shred the chicken. Grate the carrot, shred the lettuce and slice the cucumber.
Spread mayo on each wrap and add the fillings.
Roll up tightly and cut in half. Wrap in baking paper for lunchboxes.

name: Mini mince and cheese pies
blurb: Little pastry pies with savoury mince and cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Brown the mince with the diced onion.
Stir in the sauces, gravy powder and ½ cup water and simmer until thick, then cool a little.
Cut the pastry into rounds and press into a greased muffin tin.
Fill with mince, top with cheese, cover with smaller pastry rounds and brush with beaten egg.
Bake until puffed and golden.
